sources_considered.why: Primary developer survey covering productivity and confidence in shipping without human review.
Read to establish the survey's early-2025 observation period and June 12 release date. It describes the same survey, not an independent replication.
Controlled evidence of substantial coding speed gains, retained as historical context because the experiment used summer-2024 tooling.
Independent evidence cautioning against treating perceived gains as measured gains. Context only because the study's February–June observation window is not isolated to before June 16.
The July account does not clearly isolate workflows already in place by June 16.
The 2026 survey concerns a later state and cannot settle the June 2025 observation.

evidence_items.locator: Executive Summary, Productivity and quality rise together; Part 1; The confidence gap is huge
evidence_items.explanation: The early-2025 survey reports productivity gains for 78% of respondents, including large claimed gains for a subset, and low confidence alongside frequent hallucinations for 76%. It also identifies engineers confident about shipping without human review, so it supports the existence of gains and caution without establishing the exact group or categorical practice described.

The randomized experiment with 96 Google engineers estimated about 21% less task time, supporting the plausibility of substantial gains for some engineers. It studied summer-2024 tooling and does not measure their production-trust practices.

This February–June experiment found a slowdown even though participants believed AI had accelerated them, qualifying reliance on survey perceptions. Its observation window extends beyond the claim date and its specialized sample cannot disprove gains for some other engineers.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved evidence does not directly connect measured substantial speed gains with categorical refusal of unchecked production reliance in the same identified group.
Low confidence and frequent review do not establish never trusting output.
The speaker does not identify which engineers they refers to; other engineers' unchecked use cannot automatically falsify the scoped claim.
The contemporary survey measures perceived productivity rather than observed net completion time.
